title: Stress-Sharing for Decentralized Fault Repair in Modular Spacecraft
byline: [Submitted on 15 Jul 2026 (v1), last revised 21 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]
excerpt: Structural damage in modular spacecraft can disrupt mechanical and communication connectivity, reducing system capability. Existing approaches rely on redundancy or preplanned reconfiguration and do not enable autonomous repair under local information and physical constraints. We model the spacecraft as a lattice-constrained graph and introduce a fully decentralized, asynchronous stress-sharing repair policy inspired by biological wound healing: local distress signals guide surviving modules toward damaged regions to close fragmented gaps, after which each displaced module locally retraces its own motions to recover the pre-damage shape, using only local information and no absolute position sensing. We evaluate the policy in PyBullet rigid-body simulation across structures of up to 160 modules, three fault densities (10, 20, 30%), and random and localized damage. The policy consolidates the surviving modules into a single connected body: even in the most severe case tested, where 30% of modules fail at random, it gathers roughly 80% or more of the surviving modules into one connected component, and this fraction improves with assembly size, making the approach well suited as a swarm-scale repair policy for large modular spacecraft.

Abstract:Structural damage in modular spacecraft can disrupt mechanical and communication connectivity, reducing system capability. Existing approaches rely on redundancy or preplanned reconfiguration and do not enable autonomous repair under local information and physical constraints. We model the spacecraft as a lattice-constrained graph and introduce a fully decentralized, asynchronous stress-sharing repair policy inspired by biological wound healing: local distress signals guide surviving modules toward damaged regions to close fragmented gaps, after which each displaced module locally retraces its own motions to recover the pre-damage shape, using only local information and no absolute position sensing. We evaluate the policy in PyBullet rigid-body simulation across structures of up to 160 modules, three fault densities (10, 20, 30%), and random and localized damage. The policy consolidates the surviving modules into a single connected body: even in the most severe case tested, where 30% of modules fail at random, it gathers roughly 80% or more of the surviving modules into one connected component, and this fraction improves with assembly size, making the approach well suited as a swarm-scale repair policy for large modular spacecraft.

摘要：模块化航天器的结构损坏会破坏机械和通信连接，降低系统能力。 现有方法依赖于冗余或预先计划的重新配置，并且无法在本地信息和物理约束下实现自主修复。 我们将航天器建模为晶格约束图，并引入受生物伤口愈合启发的完全分散、异步压力共享修复策略：局部求救信号引导幸存模块走向受损区域以缩小碎片间隙，之后每个移位模块仅使用本地信息而不使用绝对位置感测在本地回溯其自身运动以恢复损坏前的形状。 我们在 PyBullet 刚体模拟中评估了多达 160 个模块的结构、三种故障密度（10%、20%、30%）以及随机和局部损坏的策略。 该策略将幸存的模块整合为一个连接体：即使在最严重的测试情况下，即 30% 的模块随机失效，它也会将大约 80% 或更多的幸存模块收集到一个连接的组件中，并且这一比例随着组件尺寸的增加而提高，使得该方法非常适合作为大型模块化航天器的集群规模修复策略。
